localMarshEstimates.method: Use the existing reviewed field compartment, excluding a 5 m edge strip reserved for banks and transitions. Interpolate 11.2/10.8 ft ground levels along northing, clamping beyond the two observed northings. These constrain a gently graded marsh estimate, not modern fill or a cottage-garden level.
localMarshEstimates.reason: The user identifies these marsh-edge observations as lower than the 13.9 ft Knobshill Cottage garden. Their 0.4 ft difference supports only about 12 cm northward rise; modern terrain does not justify larger interior relief.

config.outlineStatus: Provisional broad lowland envelope interpreted from the author’s 1805 marsh map, book and registered 1848–51 regional atlas. Not a surveyed marsh boundary or hydraulic boundary. Local ground evidence takes precedence.

interpolation.method: inverse distance weighting of all accepted early proxies with smooth Gaussian distance taper
interpolation.outsidePointHull: estimated continuation, explicitly not measured support

config.policy: Underlying marsh is a regional early-evidence surface across the whole lowland envelope, including later developed plots. Modern fill never supplies its interior baseline. Add later roads, yards, railways and bank/wall surfaces only within their own mapped footprints and evidence reach.
config.regionalInterpretation: Northern Hackney/Temple 14–15 ft; Stratford about 11–13 ft, with lower eastern-lane observations; northern Mill Meads about 8 ft; Abbey/Plaistow marsh generally 4–6 ft. Each estimate is representative rather than an exact floor reading.
limitations: Envelope edges are approximate. The transition is a modelling blend into adjoining non-marsh terrain, not a natural escarpment.
Southern Mill Meads has sparse early interior evidence; compare its later reviewed 7.3/7.7 ft ground readings before inferring a uniform southward drop.
River crossing by regional interpolation expresses a broad substrate trend, not flood connectivity. Surface-specific corrections remain confined to dry land.
Factory sites without usable yard readings retain an explicitly uncertain substrate estimate; a building footprint alone does not establish fill height.
config.laterGroundPolicy: Only accepted observations explicitly classified marsh, or independently reviewed ground, constrain the substrate. Unreviewed open-ground/premises and embankment-foot levels remain separate surface evidence. Corrections from the modern-derived outer model cannot propagate into the fully early-evidence interior.

policy.authority: User clarification, 2 October 2026: river, railway and sewer embankments are continuous features; map readings control profiles rather than isolated raised patches.
policy.policy: Follow the shoreline of the joined water polygons, preserving confluences and mapped open source boundaries. Associate each usable crest/wall-top observation with one nearest shoreline only. Interpolate by distance along that shoreline, including around closed island banks. Continue endpoint levels beyond the last reading. Components without their own reading use a smooth regional crest estimate from nearby eligible bank readings, explicitly marked as inferred continuation. No bank-foot or benchmark reading establishes a crest.
policy.railwayPolicy: Continuous longitudinal formation profiles on the existing mapped routes and footprints. Interpolate direct railway readings by chainage, holding endpoint readings beyond their range; retain the existing interpreted formation where no usable rail readings exist. Bridge/crossing footprints remain openings in earthworks.
policy.sewerPolicy: Full mapped centreline, flat crest and side slopes; retain the existing High Street surface-cover profile and inferred end extension. River spans are separate elevated cover surfaces and never hydraulic ground cells. This is exterior geometry, not sewer invert or flow capacity.
limitations: Continuity is a reconstruction assumption supported by mapped linear features, not a survey of every crest or breach.
Bank widths and cross-sections are interpreted. Unanchored shoreline components and long endpoint continuations remain height estimates.
The fine structural mesh is authoritative for narrow visible features; the 10 m ground raster alone cannot encode their flood-blocking topology.
Detailed-scene and hydraulic integration remain separate. No unreviewed mill/gate opening is closed.

laterSurfaceLayers.unplacedScope: All high-confidence undisputed, non-conflicted spot readings in the frozen regional audit, including locations outside the early-marsh envelope; lack of use here does not mean missing from the original TIN.
laterSurfaceLayers.policy: Surface-specific fits, not additions to general marsh controls. Continuous narrow structures are composed separately from longitudinal profiles and a fine mesh.

policy.purpose: Build the regional landscape from available evidence while further map transcription proceeds separately.

marshPrior.authority: User working expectation for marsh without better observations, 2 October 2026
marshPrior.policy: Use about 12 ft as the unsurveyed marsh prior within identified historical marsh footprints. Historical ground and ordinary street observations take precedence; banks, structures and works margins do not establish marsh height. Apply no such default to the whole valley or terrace. Blend only the outer modelling transition into adjoining relief; retain explicit estimated status.

localMarshEstimates.method: Use the existing reviewed field compartment, excluding a 5 m edge strip reserved for banks and transitions. Interpolate 11.2/10.8 ft ground levels along northing, clamping beyond the two observed northings. These constrain a gently graded marsh estimate, not modern fill or a cottage-garden level.
localMarshEstimates.reason: The user identifies these marsh-edge observations as lower than the 13.9 ft Knobshill Cottage garden. Their 0.4 ft difference supports only about 12 cm northward rise; modern terrain does not justify larger interior relief.

policy.streetPolicy: Use historical street and marsh-lane levels without a blanket fill subtraction. Adjacent ground may differ; preserve reviewed local relief.
policy.earlierMarshPolicy: Under the user's working assumption, a reviewed 1848-51 marsh-ground observation is a lower-bound estimate for 1900 where the same land surface survives. Later fill or building development may raise it. Retain original date, datum and surface role; do not treat banks, decks, benchmarks or channel beds as marsh ground. Specific evidence of excavation or a changed channel requires local review.
policy.earlierMarshStatus: Selected 1848–51 regional review now supplies 45 early low-lane and ground-margin proxies. They establish representative marsh levels under the author’s continuity assumption; they are not 45 interior marsh surveys.
policy.modernReliefPolicy: Modern relief is a fallback outside the broad historical marsh envelope only. Within that envelope the early regional marsh surface takes precedence, with later ground and bounded raised-surface evidence.
policy.boundaryPolicy: Corrections propagate only along dry grid edges that do not intersect mapped water or reviewed canal/structure exclusions. Exclusions are not hydraulic barrier heights.
policy.missingDataPolicy: Retain missing cells where neither modern terrain nor accepted historical interpolation supplies a height. No zero-height fallback.
policy.surfaceHierarchy: Regional 1848–51 marsh estimate; later ground corrections; later streets and factory yards confined to mapped footprints; bank/wall margins and railway/sewer formations confined to their own footprints. Benchmarks do not become ground or crest heights.

method: Regional marsh substrate from selected 1848–51 low-lane/ground proxies, with later ground anchors. Later street, yard, bank/wall and railway/sewer surfaces stay within mapped footprints. The partial-weight edge strip explicitly blends the solved outer surface toward the adjacent marsh residual; it is not an exact historical control surface. Outside the marsh envelope, retain the previous historical TIN and corrected 100 m broad modern prior. Correction decay length is 350 m; no correction edge crosses mapped exclusions or the boundary of the fully early-derived substrate. This source boundary does not define a hydraulic barrier. Original ground/street TIN experiment remains separate and unchanged.

limitations: Outside the mapped marsh envelope, estimated relief may retain later fill, cuttings and drainage changes; no uniform 30 cm accuracy claim.
Gaussian broad relief is a regional prior; only the historical correction is confined by the dry-edge graph.
Ten metre cells cannot resolve every narrow bank, road or drain. Structures and hydraulic connections still require reconciliation.
Early marsh support consists mostly of low-lane proxies; sparse field interiors are estimated. Datum and envelope boundaries remain provisional.

Continuous banks, railways and sewer surfaces are reconstructed along mapped features. Unsampled crest heights remain estimates; the fine mesh and the coarse raster are not yet integrated into regional flood barriers.
No missing ground is silently converted to zero elevation or a hydraulic wall.
